snip.t: Ischaemic stroke – sudden neurological deficit lasting >24 h (or until death) caused by an acute interruption of cerebral blood flow due to arterial occlusion.
Thromboembolic: Ischaemic stroke, mesenteric ischaemia, acute limb ischaemia (primarily from AF).
Systemic and Pulmonary Thromboembolism: Mural thrombus dislodgement causes ischaemic stroke, renal infarction, or limb ischaemia; deep vein thromboses lead to pulmonary embolism.
Cardiovascular events: High 5-year mortality, predominantly driven by concomitant coronary artery disease and ischaemic stroke.
